question: Should OpenClaw accept `{ owner }` records as a supported persisted shape for `plugins.slots.memory` and `plugins.slots.contextEngine` before write-side canonicalization and overwrite-invariant work exists?
rationale: This is a new config/API contract on a compatibility-sensitive plugin surface, and the canonical RFC was stale-closed without a maintainer acceptance decision.

options.title: Sponsor read-side owner records
options.body: Accept the config direction, but require the current PR to fix the concrete defects and refresh exact-head proof before merge.

options.title: Defer behind the memory-slot roadmap
options.body: Keep this branch blocked until the broader memory role-slot architecture settles which slot shapes should become public API.

options.title: Close as unaccepted direction
options.body: Reject object-form slot records for now and ask for a new RFC or maintainer-owned design before another implementation PR.

recommendation.title: Sponsor read-side owner records
recommendation.body: Accept the config direction, but require the current PR to fix the concrete defects and refresh exact-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The nearest merged maintainer-side history is plugin install slot-selection work, which is directly affected by accepting a new slot owner shape.
